event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: DLR’s 2022 filing contains an extensive dedicated subsection that squarely addresses the COVID-19 pandemic and broader epidemic risks.  The language combines forward-looking caution with descriptions of direct, already-observed impacts, such as construction delays, remote-work productivity concerns, and supply-chain interruptions.  Although no dollar amounts are given, the company repeatedly uses strong materiality qualifiers (“material and adverse impact,” “defaults by our customers,” “material adverse effect on our liquidity and financial condition”) and cites concrete operational disruptions that have already occurred (e.g., delays in deliveries to customers in specific markets).  These statements indicate an event that is both current and potentially escalating, well within the 0-3-year “recent” window; therefore, the Time Decay Principle allows higher scores.  Mitigation references (pro-active supply-chain management, remote-work policies) slightly temper overall severity but do not eliminate the fundamental exposure.  Accordingly, evidence snippets earn mid-to-high single-digit scores depending on how directly they tie COVID-19 to quantifiable or operational harm versus generic cautionary language.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business and operations, and our customers, suppliers and business partners may be adversely affected by epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemics to adverse effects on company and stakeholders.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but clear identification of pandemic risk earns a modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: Epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks of an illness, disease or virus that affect countries or regions in which we or our customers, suppliers or business partners operate, and actions taken to contain or prevent their further spread, may have a material and adverse impact on general commercial activity and on our financial condition, results of operations, liquidity and creditworthiness.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to multiple core financial metrics.
Uses strong materiality wording ('material and adverse impact').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Materiality plus coverage of liquidity and creditworthiness justify a high-moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: Epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks ... could result in significant governmental measures being implemented to control the spread of such illness ... which could adversely affect our ability and their respective abilities to adequately manage our respective businesses.

components.reason: Details specific governmental restrictions (quarantines, travel bans).
Links restrictions to management capability impairment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational pathways (government action) raise severity above generic disclosure.

evidence_list.snippet: Risks related to epidemics, pandemics or other outbreaks ... could also lead to the complete or partial closure of one or more of our offices or properties or our customers’, suppliers’ or business partners’ businesses, or otherwise result in significant disruptions to our business and operations or theirs.

components.reason: Highlights potential for facility shutdowns causing ‘significant disruptions’.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Closure of facilities is a direct operational threat deserving above-average weight.

evidence_list.snippet: Such events could materially and adversely impact our operations and the rental revenue we generate from our agreements with our customers or could result in defaults by our customers.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to rental revenue decline.
Mentions customer defaults, an acute credit risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct revenue and credit-loss exposure drives a high-moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: As with COVID-19, we may institute policies requiring employees to work remotely in certain cases and such policies may remain in place for an indeterminate amount of time or may be made mandatory by relevant government authorities.

components.reason: Notes specific remote-work shift tied to COVID-19.
Indeterminate duration increases uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational change (remote work) is specific but not directly quantified.

evidence_list.snippet: There can be no assurance that remote working arrangements will be as effective as an office environment.

components.reason: Acknowledges efficiency risk of remote work.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Secondary effect; lower but still relevant severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Moreover, pandemics or outbreaks of an illness, disease or virus could disrupt our supply chain and development activities, which could impact our ability to meet delivery timelines, including delivery timelines to our customers, and lead to delays, potential penalties that we may be required to pay and potential terminations of agreements by our customers.

components.reason: Enumerates supply-chain disruption leading to penalties and contract termination.
Specifies impact on delivery timelines and development.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Detailed operational and financial consequences warrant a high score.

evidence_list.snippet: If any such delay or disruption were to occur, it could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity and financial condition.

components.reason: Highlights liquidity risk from pandemic delays.
Uses 'material adverse effect' qualifier.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Liquidity threat with materiality language keeps score elevated.

evidence_list.snippet: In particular, the global spread of COVID-19 and the various attempts to contain it have created significant volatility, uncertainty and economic disruption.

components.reason: Directly attributes macroeconomic disruption to COVID-19.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Macro-level disruption, but not company-specific, yields mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: The global impact of the outbreak has been rapidly evolving and federal and local governments, including in locations where we operate, have responded by instituting quarantines, restrictions on travel, restrictions on the types of business that may continue to operate, and restrictions on various construction projects.

components.reason: Lists concrete government actions affecting operations.
Confirms relevance to company geographies.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Government restrictions directly relevant to construction drive moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: In response to government mandates, health care advisories and otherwise responding to employee and vendor concerns, we have altered certain aspects of our operations.

components.reason: Admits operational changes already executed.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates existing impact but lacks detail or quantified cost.

evidence_list.snippet: Our workforce, excluding our critical data center employees, is working from home, which may impact their productivity.

components.reason: Specific current remote-work status.
Raises productivity risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete operational shift with potential efficiency drawback.

evidence_list.snippet: We have also experienced delays in construction activity in a few of our markets due to government restrictions in specific locations and as a result of availability of labor and these delays are impacting some of our anticipated deliveries to our customers.

components.reason: Reports actual construction delays tied to COVID-19.
Direct effect on customer deliveries.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Actual, not hypothetical, disruption with customer impact merits high score.

evidence_list.snippet: We may continue to experience delays in construction activity, even after these restrictions are eased or lifted, due to increased safety protocols implemented in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Foresees ongoing post-pandemic delays from safety protocols.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking risk but less immediate than prior sentence.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, we cannot predict the impact that COVID-19 will have on our customers, suppliers and other business partners; however, any material effect on these parties could adversely impact us.

components.reason: Emphasises second-order exposure via counterparties.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges uncertainty, but indirect nature lowers score.

evidence_list.snippet: While we did not have any material adjustments to amounts as of and during the year ended December 31, 2021, circumstances related to the COVID-19 pandemic could potentially result in recording impairments, lease modifications and credit losses in future periods.

components.reason: Specifies possible accounting charges (impairments, credit losses).
Notes no current impact, a mitigating factor.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential but un-realized financial hits produce a balanced score.

evidence_list.snippet: The full extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic and the various responses to it impacts our business, operations and financial results will depend on numerous evolving factors that we may not be able to accurately predict...

components.reason: Highlights uncertainty and multiple impact vectors.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Broad uncertainty acknowledgement merits mid-low score.

evidence_list.snippet: During the COVID-19 pandemic, we have actively monitored our vendors and suppliers and remain in frequent communication with customers, contractors and suppliers.

components.reason: Shows active mitigation efforts (monitoring, communication).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mitigating language earns negative points under scoring rules.

evidence_list.snippet: Although to date, we have been able to manage through disruptions in our supply chain and procurement process due to the COVID-19 pandemic, continuing disruptions could have a material adverse impact on our business and financial condition.

components.reason: Admits current manageable disruptions but warns of material future impact.
Partial mitigation (‘able to manage through’).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mixed message: risk acknowledged but tempered by current success handling it.

evidence_list.snippet: However, the full extent and impact of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic on our future supply chain and procurement process cannot be reasonably estimated at this time and it could have a material adverse impact on our business and financial condition.

components.reason: States inability to estimate impact plus potential material adverse effect.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Re-emphasises uncertainty and materiality, leading to moderate score.
